standard.description: Multifunction Calibrator (original 5700A, with Option 5700A-03 and 5725A Amplifier rows)
standard.confidence_text: [Not Specified] - not printed in the manual
standard.reference: 5700A Calibrator Service Manual PN 791996, Feb 1990 Rev. 9 3/96, Chapter 1 Specifications, printed pp. 1-3 to 1-15 (PDF pp. 25-37)
standard.author: typed from the page images by specs/build_5700a_standard.py

notes.1: SOURCE: Fluke 5700A Calibrator Service Manual PN 791996, February 1990 Rev. 9, 3/96 (supplied PDF fluke--5700a--service--ID10104.pdf, 632 pages), Chapter 1 Specifications, Table 1-1, printed pp. 1-3 to 1-15 = PDF pp. 25-37 (printed 1-N = PDF N + 22). Rows carry the PDF page. This is the original 5700A; the 5700A / 5720A Series II have their own (tighter) specifications and are not covered by this sheet. Every value was read from rendered page images, not from extracted text.
notes.2: CONFIDENCE LEVEL: the manual prints none (no coverage factor or confidence interval anywhere in Chapter 1). The sheet carries no level, so the coverage divisor is 2 (k = 2 assumed, the laboratory convention for a sheet that states none). Set the divisor in Standards Specs if the manufacturer's level is confirmed from another document.
notes.3: CONDITIONS (printed pp. 1-3, 1-15): valid after a 30 minute warm-up, or twice the time the 5700A has been off; "5700A Absolute Uncertainty ... includes stability, temperature coefficient, linearity, line and load regulation, and the traceability to external standards. You do not need to add anything to absolute uncertainty". The absolute uncertainty columns are +/-5 degC from the calibration temperature (calibration 15 to 35 degC, operating 0 to 50 degC). The temperature coefficient (secondary table) is an adder only outside +/-5 degC from calibration temperature (resistance note 2, p. 1-9: or calibrated outside 19 to 24 degC). DC and AC current: for field strengths above 1 V/m but below 3 V/m add 1 % of range (pp. 1-11, 1-12): NOT included in the rows.
notes.4: PERIODS: the four absolute uncertainty columns are stored as the periods "24 hr", "90 day", "180 day" and "1 yr" (free-text period labels, the repository convention; the default period of the standard stays "1 yr"). The Relative Uncertainty columns (24 hours and 90 days, +/-1 degC) apply only after range-constant calibration and exclude the external standards: NOT stored.
notes.5: RANGE BANDS: the manual prints one specification per range, with a minimum output (DC: 0 V for every range except 100 V for the 1100 V range, p. 1-5; AC voltage and AC current: 10 % of range, p. 1-8, p. 1-13, 9 uA for the 220 uA AC current range). The sheet stores non-overlapping bands (the smallest range that holds the value, the rule the other sheets use): e.g. 2.2 V range = 0.22 V to 2.2 V, 11 V range = 2.2 V to 11 V, 22 V range = 11 V to 22 V, 1100 V range = 220 V to 1100 V. This is an interpretation, NOT verified on the instrument. The printed minimum is kept in the row's "printed" field where it differs.
notes.6: RESISTANCE (p. 1-9): the 5700A sources only fixed nominal values (1 x 10^n and 1.9 x 10^n ohm from the short to 100 Mohm). The table is the "Absolute Uncertainty of Characterized Value": the uncertainty of the value the 5700A displays, not of the nominal. Each nominal is a row whose value band is that single value (lo = hi), so a lookup finds a row only at exactly a nominal; the short (0 ohm) is a floor of 50 uohm in every column. Note 1 (p. 1-9): "Specifications apply to displayed value. 4-wire connections, except 100 mΩ" (read as printed). The characterized value may differ from nominal by up to 500 ppm (1 ohm) to 150 ppm (100 ohm to 190 kohm) (secondary table): the displayed value must be used. NOT stored: the current derating factors (p. 1-10, errors outside the allowed load current range, equations 1 and 2) and the two-wire compensation adder (4 / 15 / 60 / 120 mohm).
notes.7: AC VOLTAGE 220 V RANGE (p. 1-6): the 220 V block prints the same eight frequency bands as the lower ranges (10 Hz to 1 MHz) with the last three in % + mV. The volt-hertz capability graph (p. 1-8) and the 5700A frequency limits for 220 V do not reach 1 MHz. The rows are stored as printed; a lookup only finds them if asked for a point the instrument cannot make.
notes.8: 5725A AMPLIFIER and WIDEBAND OPTION -03: the rows printed under "5725A Amplifier:" (AC voltage 1100 V and 750 V, DC current 11 A, AC current 11 A) are stored in their own functions ("... [5725A Amplifier]"), and the Option 5700A-03 wideband module (p. 1-14, 30 Hz to 500 kHz, % of output + uV, specifications apply at the end of the cable and 50 ohm termination) in "Voltage, AC [Wideband, Option 5700A-03]". specmanager.DEFAULT_VARIANT excludes "5725a" and "wideband" from a plain lookup, so the base 5700A figures are used unless variant= asks for them. Amplifier AC voltage bands are 10 % to 100 % of the range (minimum output, p. 1-8), interpretation.
notes.9: FREQUENCY: the manual prints one figure, "Uncertainty: +/-0.01 %" (p. 1-8 AC voltage, p. 1-13 AC current, p. 1-14 wideband), with no period. Stored under "1 yr" only (the same choice as the 5520A sheet); no 24 hr / 90 day / 180 day value was invented. Ranges 10.000-11.999 Hz ... 120.0k-1.1999 MHz, resolution 11 999 counts (so 0.001 Hz up to 100 Hz per range digit); wideband resolution 11 999 counts to 1.1999 MHz, 119 counts to 30 MHz.
notes.10: NOT STORED: relative uncertainty columns; secondary performance tables (stability, temperature coefficient, noise, linearity, load regulation, distortion, compliance limits, burden voltage adder, maximum load / peak current); resistance current derating and two-wire adders; wideband flatness (flatness to a 1 kHz reference: 10 Hz to 30 MHz, +/- 0.1 % to 1.5 % + uV) and harmonic distortion; phase lock and phase reference specifications; settling times.

limits.limit: 0 to +/-1100 V; minimum output 0 V on every range except 100 V on the 1100 V range. Maximum load 50 mA (2.2 V to 220 V ranges), 20 mA (1100 V); 50 ohm output impedance on the 220 mV range. Remote sensing available 0 to +/-1100 V on the 2.2 V to 1100 V ranges.

10 Hz to 1.2 MHz (5700A, mV ranges to 1 MHz in the table); 1100 V range 50 Hz to 1 kHz on the 5700A alone; 5725A amplifier 1100 V from 40 Hz to 30 kHz and 750 V from 30 kHz to 100 kHz; volt-hertz limit 2.2 x 10^7 V-Hz; minimum output 10 % of range; maximum load 50 mA (2.2 V to 220 V, 0 to 40 degC), 20 mA (40 to 50 degC), 6 mA (1100 V); external sense below 100 kHz (5700A), below 30 kHz (5725A).
300 uV (-57 dBm) to 3.5 V (+24 dBm), 10 Hz to 30 MHz; absolute uncertainty specified 30 Hz to 500 kHz; dBm reference 50 ohm; frequency uncertainty +/-0.01 %.
0 to 2.2 A from the 5700A terminals (11 A with the 5725A); minimum output 0 on every range; 5700A compliance 2 V for outputs from 1 A to 2.2 A; maximum from the 5700A terminals 2.2 A.

10 Hz to 10 kHz (2.2 A range from 20 Hz; 5725A 11 A range from 40 Hz); maximum 2.2 A from the 5700A (11 A with the 5725A, minimum 1 A); minimum output 9 uA on the 220 uA range, 10 % on the other ranges; power factor 0.9 to 1 (5700A), 0.1 to 1 (5725A); inductive load 400 uH (20 uH above 1 A).

1 x 10^n and 1.9 x 10^n ohm from the short to 100 Mohm (fixed values, no continuously variable output); load current ranges 8-500 mA (short) down to 50-200 nA (100 Mohm); two-wire compensation for values below 100 kohm, limited to 11 mA and 2 V burden.

Warm-up twice the time since last warmed up, to a maximum of 30 minutes; operating 0 to 50 degC, calibration 15 to 35 degC, storage -40 to 75 degC; guard isolation 20 V; interfaces IEEE-488, RS-232, 5725A, 5205A / 5215A, 5220A, phase lock in (BNC), phase reference out (BNC); line 47 to 63 Hz, +/-10 % of the selected nominal 100 / 110 / 115 / 120 / 200 / 220 / 230 / 240 V, maximum 300 VA (5700A), 750 VA (5725A).

Typed from the 5700A Service Manual Rev. 9 (3/96) specification tables (printed pp. 1-5 to 1-15); no approval signature. The manual prints NO confidence level: the sheet has none (divisor 2, k = 2 assumed). The original 5700A only; the 5700A Series II specifications are different.

problems.where: Voltage, AC [Sinewave] / 2.2 mV and 22 mV @ 500 kHz to 1 MHz
problems.what: The 90 day absolute uncertainty is printed ".44% + 4" (p. 1-6); the 24 hour, 180 day and 1 year cells of the same row print "+ 40" and the 24 hour limit is already ".4% + 40". Stored as printed (4 uV); almost certainly a missing zero.
The 220 V block prints the same eight frequency bands as the lower ranges, up to 500 kHz to 1 MHz (p. 1-6); the volt-hertz limit does not allow it. Stored as printed (note 7).

problems.where: Voltage, AC [Sinewave] / 220 V @ 100 kHz to 300 kHz
problems.what: The 90 day absolute uncertainty is ".15% + 110" like the 24 hour column; the relative column prints ".15% + 100" (not stored). Stored as printed.
The manual prints "Minimum output: 0 V for all ranges, except 100 V for 1100 V range" (p. 1-5); the sheet stores non-overlapping bands (note 5). Interpretation, not verified on the instrument.
The 5700A 1100 V range prints 50 Hz to 1 kHz only; stored from 220 V (the top of the 220 V range) although its printed minimum output is 10 % of range (110 V).
The 24 hour column prints "15 + 500" (p. 1-14), larger than the 90 day cell ".2 + 500": almost certainly ".15 + 500". The 24 hr period of this row is NOT stored.
Fixed nominal values only (note 6): a lookup finds a row only at exactly a nominal. The two-wire compensation adder and the current derating factors (p. 1-10) are NOT included.

Note 1 of the resistance table is printed "4-wire connections, except 100 mΩ"; it may mean the 100 Mohm nominal (the one value with no 4-wire hook-up). Read as printed, not interpreted; check against the Operator Manual.
The manual prints one frequency uncertainty (+/-0.01 %) with no period; stored under "1 yr" (note 9).
Not stored: relative uncertainty columns, secondary performance tables, resistance derating factors, wideband flatness and harmonics, phase specifications (note 10).
